:::{#lem-bernoulli-precision-deriv}
#### Derivative of the Bernoulli precision

If $\Outvar$ is a [Bernoulli](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-bernoulli) variable, $\Outvar \sim \Ber(\prob)$ with $\prob \in (0, 1)$
and [precision](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/variance-covariance.html#def-precision) $\precision = 1 / \paren{\prob(1 - \prob)}$,
then the derivative of $\precision$ with respect to $\prob$ is

$$\deriv{\prob} \precision = -\sqf{\precision} \paren{1 - 2 \prob}$$

:::

::: proof

The derivative needs the chain rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\deriv{\prob} \precision
&= \deriv{\prob} \paren{\prob(1 - \prob)}^{-1}
&& \text{(definition of $\precision$ as a negative power)}\\
&= \deriv{\prob} \paren{\prob - \sqf{\prob}}^{-1}
&& \text{(distribute $\prob$)}\\
&= -\paren{\prob - \sqf{\prob}}^{-2} \deriv{\prob} \paren{\prob - \sqf{\prob}}
&& \text{(chain rule and power rule)}\\
&= -\paren{\prob - \sqf{\prob}}^{-2} \paren{1 - 2 \prob}
&& \text{(linearity and power rule)}\\
&= -\paren{\prob(1 - \prob)}^{-2} \paren{1 - 2 \prob}
&& \text{(factor $\prob - \sqf{\prob} = \prob(1 - \prob)$)}\\
&= -\sqf{\precision} \paren{1 - 2 \prob}
&& \text{(definition of $\precision$)}
\end{aligned}
$$

:::
